source: Government of India — myScheme.gov.in / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)
schemes.description: Central Sector Scheme providing income support to all landholding farmer families across India to supplement their financial needs for agricultural inputs and household expenses.
benefits: Financial benefit of ₹6,000 per year transferred directly to bank account (DBT).
Paid in three equal 4-monthly installments of ₹2,000 each (April-July, August-November, December-March).
Aadhaar-seeded direct benefit transfer with zero middlemen commission.
eligibility: All landholding farmer families having cultivable landholding in their names.
Must have Aadhaar card linked with active bank account and NPCI mapped.
eKYC completion on PM-KISAN portal is mandatory.

Exclusions: Institutional landholders, constitutional post holders, serving/retired government employees, income tax payees of last assessment year, and professionals (doctors, engineers, lawyers, CAs).
documentsRequired: Aadhaar Card of the applicant farmer
Land ownership document (e.g. 7/12 extract / RoR / Khatauni / Khasra)
Active mobile number linked with Aadhaar for OTP verification
applicationProcess: Visit the official PM-KISAN portal (pmkisan.gov.in) or visit nearest Common Service Center (CSC).
Click on 'Farmer Corner' → 'New Farmer Registration'.
Enter Aadhaar Number, select State, and verify OTP sent to Aadhaar-registered mobile.
Fill in land details (District, Sub-District, Block, Village, Survey/Khata/Khasra number, Area in hectares).
Upload scanned land record copy and submit the application for State Nodal verification.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
schemes.description: Flagship comprehensive crop insurance scheme providing financial support and risk cover against non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest stages.
benefits: Very low uniform premium rate for farmers: only 2.0% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi food & oilseed crops, and 5% for annual commercial/horticultural crops.
Government of India and State Government subsidize the remaining actuarial premium equally.
Full insured sum claim payout without capping or reduction for notified areas.
Coverage for prevented sowing, mid-season adversity, localized calamities (hailstorm, landslide, inundation), and post-harvest losses up to 14 days.
eligibility: All farmers including sharecroppers and tenant farmers growing notified crops in notified areas.
Both loanee farmers (compulsory/automatic through banks unless opted out) and non-loanee farmers (voluntary).
Application must be submitted before the prescribed cut-off date for Kharif or Rabi seasons.
documentsRequired: Land Record Document (7/12 extract / RoR / Land Possession Certificate)
Crop Sowing Certificate / Self-declaration of crop sown
Bank Passbook copy with IFSC & Account Number
Tenant agreement / declaration in case of sharecropper/tenant farmer
applicationProcess: Log in to the official National Crop Insurance Portal (pmfby.gov.in) or Crop Insurance mobile app.
Loanee farmers are automatically covered through their crop loan bank branch unless opted out.
Non-loanee farmers can apply online directly or via nearest CSC/Bank branch before season cut-off date.
Select State, Season (Kharif/Rabi), Year, Scheme, and enter farmer details.
Enter survey number, area sown, crop name, and pay the subsidized farmer premium online.
schemes.maxSubsidyAmount: Up to 100% Sum Insured based on yield loss

schemes.name: PMKSY — Per Drop More Crop (Micro Irrigation)
schemes.description: Component of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana focusing on enhancing water use efficiency at farm level through Drip and Sprinkler micro-irrigation systems.
benefits: Subsidy of up to 55% of indicative cost for Small and Marginal farmers.
Subsidy of up to 45% of indicative cost for Other farmers.
Additional top-up assistance of 10-20% provided by various State Governments (e.g. Maharashtra MahaDBT gives up to 75-80% total subsidy).
Reduces water consumption by 30-50% and increases crop productivity by 20-40%.
eligibility: All categories of farmers having cultivable land with an assured water source (well, borewell, canal, farm pond).
Members of cooperative farming societies, self-help groups, and water user associations are also eligible.
Land should have clear title or lease agreement for at least 7 years.
documentsRequired: Water Source Certificate / electricity bill of pump set
Quotation / proforma invoice from empaneled micro-irrigation manufacturer
applicationProcess: Apply through State Agricultural Portal (e.g. MahaDBT in Maharashtra: mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in, or PMKSY portal).
Select 'Micro Irrigation (Drip/Sprinkler)' under Agriculture Schemes.
Upload required land and water source documents and choose registered system vendor.
Field inspection by agricultural officer followed by administrative approval (pre-sanction).
Install system and upload post-installation geo-tagged inspection report for subsidy release to bank account.

schemes.name: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM)
schemes.description: National scheme aimed at increasing farm power reach and mechanization among small and marginal farmers by providing subsidies on agricultural equipment and custom hiring centers.
benefits: 40% to 50% financial assistance for individual farmers to purchase tractors, power tillers, rotavators, seed drills, sprayers, harvesters, and threshers.
Up to ₹10 Lakh subsidy (40-80%) for establishing Custom Hiring Centers (CHCs) by farmer groups, FPOs, and rural youth.
Special higher subsidy percentage for women farmers, SC/ST farmers, and North-Eastern region farmers.
eligibility: Farmers of all landholding categories registered on the Agriboost/FARMS mechanization portal.
Priority given to Small & Marginal farmers, women farmers, and SC/ST beneficiaries.
Applicant should not have availed government subsidy for the same category machine in the past 5-7 years.
documentsRequired: Caste certificate (if applicable for enhanced subsidy)
Dealer quotation from authorized agricultural machinery manufacturers
applicationProcess: Register on the official mechanization portal (agrimachinery.nic.in) or State DBT portal.
Select machinery type (Tractor, Rotavator, Multi-crop Thresher, Power Weeder, Drone, etc.).
Select authorized dealer and submit application with land documents.
Upon lottery/merit selection and pre-sanction verification, purchase the machine from the empaneled dealer.
Physical verification and geotagging by Department of Agriculture triggers direct subsidy release.

schemes.name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme
schemes.description: Provides adequate and timely credit support to farmers under a single window with flexible and simplified procedures for cultivation expenses and working capital.
benefits: Short-term crop cultivation loan up to ₹3 Lakh at an attractive concessional interest rate of 7% p.a.
Interest Subvention of 3% for prompt repayment, resulting in an effective interest rate of only 4.0% per annum.
Collateral-free agricultural loan limit up to ₹1.60 Lakh without hypothecation or mortgage.
Extended to Animal Husbandry, Dairy, and Fisheries farmers for working capital up to ₹2 Lakh within overall ₹3 Lakh ceiling.
eligibility: Individual farmers / joint borrowers who are owner cultivators.
Tenant farmers, oral lessees, and sharecroppers.
Self Help Groups (SHGs) or Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) of farmers.
documentsRequired: Identity Proof (Aadhaar Card / Voter ID / PAN Card)
Land Records (7/12 extract / Patta / Khasra) showing cropping pattern
applicationProcess: Download one-page KCC application form from PM-KISAN portal (pmkisan.gov.in) or public sector bank website.
Fill basic landholding details, crop sown, and bank account number.
Submit the form along with land documents to nearest Commercial Bank, Cooperative Bank, or RRB branch.
Bank issues KCC smart card / debit card within 14 days of document verification.
schemes.maxSubsidyAmount: Effective 4% interest rate on up to ₹3 Lakh

schemes.name: Soil Health Card Scheme
schemes.description: Nationwide scheme that issues soil health report cards to farmers every 2 years, providing customized nutrient status and crop-wise fertilizer dosage recommendations.
benefits: Free scientific testing of soil samples for 12 key parameters (N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, Bo, pH, EC, OC).
Crop-wise fertilizer dosage recommendations to eliminate excessive chemical usage and cut cultivation costs by 15-25%.
Customized soil amendment advice (gypsum, lime, organic compost) for alkaline or acidic soil rehabilitation.
eligibility: All farmers across all States and Union Territories in India.
No land size restriction.
documentsRequired: Land Record details (Khata / Survey Number / Village)
applicationProcess: Soil samples are collected by agriculture extension officers or Village Knowledge Centers following grid methodology.
Farmers can also self-collect representative soil samples and deposit them at nearest Soil Testing Laboratory (STL) or KVK.
Track sample testing status and download Soil Health Card online from soilhealth.dac.gov.in.

schemes.name: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)
schemes.description: Promotes organic farming through cluster approach and Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) certification, supporting chemical-free sustainable agriculture.
benefits: Financial assistance of ₹50,000 per hectare for a 3-year cycle.
₹31,000/ha provided directly through DBT to the farmer for organic inputs (seeds, bio-fertilizers, vermicompost, bio-pesticides).
₹8,800/ha for value addition, packaging, labelling, and organic branding.
Free Participatory Guarantee System (PGS-India) organic certification.
eligibility: Farmers forming farmer clusters of 20 hectares or 50 farmers within contiguous agricultural area.
Individual farmers willing to adopt organic agricultural package of practices over a minimum 3-year transition.
applicationProcess: Form a group of 20-50 farmers in the village and approach the Block / Taluka Agriculture Officer (DAO).
Register the cluster on Jaivik Kheti portal (jaivikkheti.in).
Undergo PGS-India training, implement organic input protocol, and receive DBT input assistance.

schemes.name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
schemes.description: Medium-long term debt financing facility for investment in viable post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets.
benefits: 3.0% per annum interest subvention on loans up to ₹2.00 Crore for a maximum tenure of 7 years.
Credit guarantee coverage under CGTMSE for loans up to ₹2.00 Crore with government-paid fee.
Eligible projects: Warehouses, cold storages, pack-houses, sorting & grading units, primary processing facilities, solar dryers, and ripening chambers.
eligibility: Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Marketing Cooperative Societies, FPOs, SHGs, JLGs, Farmers, Agri-entrepreneurs, and Start-ups.
applicationProcess: Register on the official AIF portal (agriinfra.dac.gov.in).
Submit online loan application with project details and select preferred lending bank.
Ministry evaluates within 7 days and forwards to the chosen bank for sanction and interest subvention mapping.

schemes.name: Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Nidhi Yojana (Maharashtra)
schemes.description: Maharashtra State Government top-up scheme providing supplementary income assistance to all PM-KISAN verified beneficiary farmers in Maharashtra.
benefits: Additional ₹6,000 per year financial benefit directly from Maharashtra State Government.
Combined with PM-KISAN, eligible farmers in Maharashtra receive a total of ₹12,000 per year.
Paid in three equal installments of ₹2,000 each linked with PM-KISAN payout cycles.
eligibility: Farmer must be an active, verified beneficiary of the PM-KISAN scheme in Maharashtra.
Land must be situated within the State of Maharashtra.
Aadhaar-seeded bank account and active eKYC required.
documentsRequired: Bank Account details linked with NPCI
applicationProcess: Beneficiaries already receiving PM-KISAN in Maharashtra are enrolled automatically without separate application.
Check payment and verification status on the official MahaDBT portal (mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in) or Department of Agriculture Maharashtra portal.

schemes.name: Mukhyamantri Saur Krushi Pump Yojana (Magel Tyala Solar Pump)
schemes.description: Flagship scheme of Maharashtra State providing off-grid solar-powered agriculture water pump sets (3 HP, 5 HP, 7.5 HP) at heavy government subsidy.
benefits: Up to 90% subsidy for General category farmers (farmer pays only 10% of total cost).
Up to 95% subsidy for SC / ST category farmers (farmer pays only 5% of total cost).
Provides reliable daytime irrigation electricity for 25 years with free 5-year maintenance and remote monitoring.
eligibility: Farmers with agricultural land possessing an assured water source (dug well, borewell, farm pond, river).
Farmers who do not have conventional grid electrical connection for agriculture pump.
Land holding: Up to 2.5 acres eligible for 3 HP pump; 2.5 to 5 acres for 5 HP pump; >5 acres for 7.5 HP pump.
documentsRequired: 7/12 Extract with crop and water source entry
Aadhaar Card and Caste Certificate (if applicable)
NOC from co-owners if land is joint ownership
applicationProcess: Apply online on the MSEDCL / MahaDiscom Solar Portal (kisan.mahadiscom.in) or MahaDBT.
Fill farmer details, land survey number, and select pump capacity (3/5/7.5 HP).
Upload 7/12 extract and Aadhaar card, and pay farmer contribution online upon survey approval.
Authorized solar vendor installs pump and solar panel array within 30-45 days.

schemes.name: Magel Tyala Shettale (Farm Pond on Demand - Maharashtra)
schemes.description: Maharashtra Government initiative to provide financial subsidy directly to individual farmers for constructing on-farm water storage ponds (Shettale) with plastic lining.
benefits: Direct financial grant of up to ₹50,000 to ₹75,000 for farm pond excavation.
Additional subsidy of up to ₹1,00,000 for 500-micron plastic film lining to prevent seepage.
Ensures critical protective irrigation during dry spells during Kharif and Rabi seasons.
eligibility: Farmer must possess at least 0.60 hectare (1.5 acres) of cultivable agricultural land.
The proposed site should be technically feasible for rainwater harvesting / runoff storage.
Individual farmer must not have availed farm pond subsidy earlier.
applicationProcess: Apply on MahaDBT portal (mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in) under Farmer Schemes → Special Irrigation Category.
Department agriculture officer inspects the site and issues pre-sanction letter.
Complete excavation through JCB/machinery and upload geo-tagged photograph on the portal.
Post-completion measurement by Taluka Agriculture Officer triggers direct DBT grant release.

schemes.name: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)
schemes.description: Centrally sponsored scheme for holistic growth of horticulture sector covering fruits, vegetables, root and tuber crops, mushrooms, spices, flowers, and aromatic plants.
benefits: 40% to 50% subsidy on shade net houses, polyhouses, plastic mulching, and anti-hail nets.
Financial support of up to ₹40,000/ha for establishing new fruit orchards (Mango, Pomegranate, Guava, Citrus, etc.).
Subsidies on post-harvest pack-houses, cold rooms, and refrigerated transport vans.
eligibility: Individual farmers, farmer groups, FPOs, and cooperatives engaged in horticultural crop production.
Farmer must own suitable land with assured irrigation.
documentsRequired: 7/12 Extract / Land Record showing suitability for horticulture
Technical quotation from empanelled polyhouse / nursery vendor
applicationProcess: Apply on National Horticulture Mission portal (midh.gov.in) or State Horticulture DBT portal.
Select sub-scheme component (Protected Cultivation, New Orchard, Cold Storage, etc.).
Submit project proposal and receive pre-sanction approval from District Horticulture Officer.
Complete installation and obtain verification for subsidy disbursement.

schemes.name: National Agriculture Market (e-NAM)
schemes.description: Pan-India electronic trading portal networking existing APMC mandis to create a unified national market for agricultural commodities with transparent price discovery.
benefits: Access to nationwide buyers and traders directly from local APMC mandi without intermediaries.
Real-time online bidding for agricultural produce ensuring better price discovery.
Direct online payment into farmer's bank account upon sale confirmation.
Free quality assaying and testing facilities at participating mandis.
eligibility: Any farmer bringing agricultural produce to an e-NAM integrated APMC market.
No registration fees.
applicationProcess: Register online at enam.gov.in or at the e-NAM registration desk at any connected APMC mandi.
Obtain farmer registration ID and weigh/assay produce at arrival gate.
Lot goes live for online electronic bidding by traders across India.
Accept the highest bid and receive payment directly in bank account.

schemes.name: National Livestock Mission (NLM)
schemes.description: National scheme aimed at sustainable development of the livestock sector with focus on breed improvement, feed & fodder availability, and livestock entrepreneurship.
benefits: 50% capital subsidy (up to ₹50 Lakh) for establishing goat, sheep, piggery, and poultry breeding farms.
50% capital subsidy (up to ₹50 Lakh) for fodder production units (silage making, total mixed ration, fodder block units).
Subsidized livestock insurance coverage against accidental death and disease.
eligibility: Individual farmers, rural entrepreneurs, FPOs, SHGs, and Section 8 companies.
Applicant must have trained manpower or undergo mandatory livestock training.
documentsRequired: Land Record / Lease agreement for shed construction
Bank loan sanction letter (for remaining 50% project cost)
Training certificate from recognized veterinary institute
applicationProcess: Apply online on the NLM portal (nlm.udyamimitra.in).
Submit project proposal, land records, and select lending bank.
State Level Executive Committee screens application and sanctions 50% DBT capital subsidy released in two equal tranches.
